plan.question: Full typed 64-bit and 32-bit mask reduction overloads on complete physical wave64 groups

plan.limitations: Mask type and full-mask bit value both differ. The two API contracts request different semantic groups; not a fixed-value type-only causal comparison or speedup test. Complete active physical waves only.

artifacts.public_projection: 62 cases and all 620 raw timing batches; all 27840 payload plus 3968 guard words from device files; 128 source words once; both build modes, raw-derived trace names/durations/resources, cache counts, and sanitized allocation/release observations

limitations: The comparison changes both the mask argument type and its full-mask bit value; it is not a fixed-value type-only intervention.
Per-channel group_width is the declared expected API semantic group, not a measured change in the physical runtime wave size.
Complete physical wave64 groups execute all collectives; logical tails are zero-valued inputs, not inactive physical threads.
No arbitrary or sparse mask, zero mask, early-exit, inactive source, partial physical wave, down-shuffle, xor or vote qualification.
The unchanged nine-channel regression is auxiliary; its timing is not compared with the two-channel primary kernel as a speedup.
Descriptive event/host batches include complete kernels and possible submission gaps, not per-intrinsic latency or throughput.
Only final outputs of repeated launches are saved; intermediate invocations were not individually checked.
Correctness does not establish a native hardware reduction instruction or a shared-memory ordering guarantee.
Trace resource fields, cache file counts and recompile flags do not establish actual residency, physical allocation or compilation counts.
One C550/software stack and deterministic int32 input; no floating-point or target-framework qualification.
